paragraphs.text: The preceding elements of a problem can be gathered into a single data structure that is given as input to a problem-solving algorithm. A solution to a problem is an action sequence that leads from the initial state to a goal state. Solution quality is measured by the path cost function, and an optimal solution has the lowest path cost among all solutions.

Uniform-cost search does not care about the number of steps a path has, but only about their total cost. Therefore, it will get stuck in an infinite loop if there is a path with an infinite sequence of zero-cost actions—for example, a sequence of NoOp actions. Completeness is guaranteed provided the cost of every step exceeds some small positive constant ε.
